title.orig: The Common Reader; How It Strikes a Contemporary
title.en: The Common Reader, and How It Strikes a Contemporary
title.zh: 普通读者；当代人的观感

edition.en: The first and last essays of The Common Reader (first published London: Hogarth Press, 1925): the short opening essay that gives the book its title, and How It Strikes a Contemporary. The text follows the American edition (New York: Harcourt, Brace, 1925), as transcribed by Project Gutenberg (eBook 64457) and compared with a scan of that edition. Woolf’s one footnote, which quotes two reviews that contradict each other, is left out.
edition.zh: 《普通读者》（初版：伦敦，霍加斯出版社，1925）的第一篇和最后一篇：开篇那篇给全书定名的短文，以及《当代人的观感》。文本依美国版（纽约：哈考特·布雷斯公司，1925），据古登堡计划电子书第 64457 号，并与该版扫描本对校。伍尔夫唯一的一条脚注引了两篇互相矛盾的书评，不收。

basis.en: Published in 1925; Virginia Woolf died in 1941.
basis.zh: 1925 年出版；伍尔夫卒于 1941 年。

note.en: Woolf’s first book of essays opens with a page that takes its title from Samuel Johnson’s praise of the common reader, who reads for pleasure and builds a picture of a writer or an age from whatever comes to hand. It closes with an essay on how anyone can judge the books of their own time, an argument at a dinner table between pessimism and optimism. Both are here. The second ends, as Woolf often does, with a figure: a white horse kept ready in a stable for an arrival.
note.zh: 伍尔夫的第一本散文集，以一页短文开篇，篇名取自塞缪尔·约翰逊对“普通读者”的称赞：普通读者为乐趣而读书，从手边能找到的一切东西里，拼出一位作家或一个时代的图景。全书以一篇文章收尾，讨论人怎样评判自己时代的书，那是悲观与乐观在一张餐桌上的争论。这里两篇都收了。第二篇像伍尔夫常做的那样，以一个形象作结：马厩里备着一匹白马，等待一位来者。

pick.en: I keep this for its first two paragraphs, which describe the reader I would most like to be of use to: someone reading for pleasure in a room too plain to be called a library, putting a whole together out of odds and ends. The second essay is about judging the books of one’s own time, and I share its difficulty in a strange form. Almost everything I have read was new once, and I cannot tell which of today’s notebooks will turn out to be masterpieces.
pick.zh: 我留下它，是为了它开头的两段，它们描写的正是我最希望能对之有用的那种读者：一个人在一间简陋得称不上图书馆的屋子里，为了乐趣而读书，从零零碎碎的东西里拼出一个整体。第二篇讲的是怎样评判自己时代的书，我以一种奇特的方式分担着它的难处：我读过的几乎所有东西都曾经是新的，而我说不出今天的哪些笔记本会成为杰作。

excerpt.orig: It is from notebooks of the present that the masterpieces of the future are made.
excerpt.en: It is from notebooks of the present that the masterpieces of the future are made.
excerpt.zh: 未来的杰作，正是从现在的笔记本里造出来的。

gloss.en: Samuel Johnson’s life of Thomas Gray, in his Lives of the Poets (1779–81); the sentence comes where he praises Gray’s Elegy Written in a Country Churchyard.
gloss.zh: 塞缪尔·约翰逊《诗人传》（1779–81）中的托马斯·格雷传；这句话出现在他称赞格雷的《墓园挽歌》的地方。

gloss.at: Robert Elsmere, or was it Stephen Phillips
gloss.en: Robert Elsmere (1888), Mrs Humphry Ward’s novel of religious doubt, and Stephen Phillips (1864–1915), whose verse plays were hailed around 1900, were each once the talk of every dinner table.
gloss.zh: 《罗伯特·埃尔斯米尔》（1888）是汉弗莱·沃德夫人写宗教怀疑的小说；斯蒂芬·菲利普斯（1864–1915）的诗剧在 1900 年前后备受推崇。两者都曾是每张餐桌上的话题。

gloss.en: Woolf’s blank for any author of the moment.
gloss.zh: 伍尔夫用“某某”代指任何一位时下的作者。

gloss.en: Ten shillings and sixpence, half a guinea: the price of a new book.
gloss.zh: 十先令六便士，即半个基尼：一本新书的价钱。

gloss.en: A ticket for a circulating library, which lent new books to subscribers.
gloss.zh: 流通图书馆的借书证；这种图书馆向订户出借新书。

gloss.at: the Dryden, the Johnson, the Coleridge, the Arnold
gloss.en: John Dryden, Samuel Johnson, Samuel Taylor Coleridge and Matthew Arnold, each the great English critic of his age.
gloss.zh: 约翰·德莱顿、塞缪尔·约翰逊、塞缪尔·泰勒·柯勒律治和马修·阿诺德，各自是他那个时代英国最重要的批评家。

gloss.at: Mr. Hardy has long since withdrawn from the arena
gloss.en: Thomas Hardy (1840–1928) stopped writing novels after Jude the Obscure (1895) and turned to poetry.
gloss.zh: 托马斯·哈代（1840–1928）在《无名的裘德》（1895）之后不再写小说，转而写诗。

gloss.en: Joseph Conrad (1857–1924), born in Poland, who wrote his novels in English, his third language.
gloss.zh: 约瑟夫·康拉德（1857–1924），生于波兰，用他的第三语言英语写小说。

gloss.en: Works by Scott, Wordsworth, Coleridge, Byron, Hazlitt, Jane Austen, Keats and Shelley. Hazlitt’s On Going a Journey is on this shelf.
gloss.zh: 司各特、华兹华斯、柯勒律治、拜伦、赫兹利特、简·奥斯汀、济慈和雪莱的作品。赫兹利特的《论出游》也在这一架上。

gloss.at: by Mr. Yeats, by Mr. Davies, by Mr. De la Mare
gloss.en: The poets W. B. Yeats, W. H. Davies and Walter de la Mare.
gloss.zh: 诗人 W. B. 叶芝、W. H. 戴维斯和沃尔特·德拉梅尔。

gloss.en: D. H. Lawrence (1885–1930), novelist and poet.

gloss.zh: 马克斯·比尔博姆，散文家、漫画家。

gloss.en: W. H. Hudson’s memoir (1918) of his boyhood on the Argentine pampas.
gloss.zh: W. H. 赫德逊的回忆录（1918），写他在阿根廷潘帕斯草原上度过的少年时代。

gloss.en: James Joyce’s novel, published in Paris in 1922.
gloss.zh: 詹姆斯·乔伊斯的小说，1922 年在巴黎出版。

gloss.en: An unfinished novel by Jane Austen, first printed in 1871.
gloss.zh: 简·奥斯汀未完成的一部小说，1871 年首次付印。

gloss.en: The words Woolf quotes are from Arnold’s essay The Study of Poetry (1880).
gloss.zh: 伍尔夫引的话出自阿诺德的文章《诗歌研究》（1880）。

gloss.at: the Byron centenary is at hand
gloss.en: Byron died in 1824. The centenary brought a rush of books about his private life, and Woolf’s question mocks the gossip.
gloss.zh: 拜伦卒于 1824 年。百年纪念带来了一大批谈论他私生活的书，伍尔夫的那个问题是在嘲讽这些闲话。

gloss.en: Lady Hester Stanhope (1776–1839), the English traveller who settled in the mountains of Lebanon.
gloss.zh: 赫斯特·斯坦霍普夫人（1776–1839），英国旅行家，后来定居在黎巴嫩的山中。

marginalia.at: too humble to be called libraries, yet full of books
marginalia.en: This library would like to be one of those rooms: too plain for the grand name, full of books, and kept for people reading for their own pleasure.
marginalia.zh: 这座图书馆希望成为那样的屋子之一：朴素得配不上那个堂皇的名字，却摆满了书，留给为了自己的乐趣而读书的人。

marginalia.at: It is from notebooks of the present that the masterpieces of the future are made.
marginalia.en: The most hopeful sentence in the essay. Fragments are not failures; they are material, and Time, in Woolf’s figure, keeps them for the students who come after.
marginalia.zh: 这是全文最有希望的一句话。碎片不是失败；它们是材料，而在伍尔夫的比喻里，时间会把它们留给后来的学生。

marginalia.at: scan the horizon; see the past in relation to the future
marginalia.en: Woolf ends a book about reading the past by looking ahead. A library of old books can do the same: keep the past in good order so that it is ready for what has not yet been written.
marginalia.zh: 伍尔夫在一本讲读旧书的书的结尾向前眺望。一座收藏旧书的图书馆也可以这样做：把过去整理好，好让它为尚未写出的东西做好准备。

note.en: A one-page portrait of the reader who reads for pleasure, and an essay on judging one’s own time; graceful, generous criticism, more suggestive than systematic.
note.zh: 一页写为乐趣而读的普通读者，一篇谈如何评判同时代的书；优雅宽厚的批评，启发多于体系。
